result.topic_en: Draft Latin theses accompanying Riemann's dissertation, listing points where his definition of a complex function, his theorem in art. 12, and his method of determining complex functions differ from views of other authors such as Cauchy.
result.transcription:

items.quote:
Hanc rem qui ante nos attigerunt, ita
a nobis, quantum scimus, abhorrent,
ut [-aut-] proprietatem, qua nos ad defini-

items.english: Those who touched on this matter before us differ from us, as far as we know, in that they either did not attribute to it at all the property by which we defined this notion (as the illustrious Cauchy, Comptes rendus), or did not include it in the definition.

items.quote:
„Wenn eine Function $w$ von $z$ ec“
{+Cui+} [-Huic-] repugnat sententia Ill. Cauchy [-in-]
(Comptes rendus ) {+pronuntiata+}.
items.english: The theorem 'If a function w of z ...' is contradicted by the opinion pronounced by the illustrious Cauchy (Comptes rendus).

items.quote:
Tertius qui hic notandus videtur
locus est de determinatione functionis
complexae quantitatis variabilis.
items.english: The third point that seems worth noting here concerns the determination of a function of a complex variable.
